items.text: The Nifty fell about 2.1% and the Sensex about 2.3% over the week, their fifth straight weekly decline, as foreign investors kept selling into the crude oil spike and rising global yields.
The rupee had its sharpest weekly fall in four months, sliding to around 95.5-95.6 per dollar as Brent crude briefly approached $110, with the RBI stepping in to sell dollars to slow the decline.

India's 10-year bond yield pushed past 7% for the first time in a while, as the RBI trimmed bond buybacks even while draining roughly Rs 1 trillion to Rs 1.5 lakh crore of surplus cash through OMO bond sales and VRRR auctions over the week.

Retail inflation is estimated to have risen to a 20-month high near 4.9% in August, narrowing the room for an RBI rate cut; SBI's research arm now expects 25 basis-point hikes in both October and December instead.
India's forex reserves jumped $44.9 billion in a week to a record $785.7 billion, the world's fourth largest, giving the RBI more firepower to keep defending the rupee into next week.
US consumer inflation rose 3.4% year-on-year in August, flipping market expectations from a Fed rate cut to an almost-certain hike at next week's meeting, with odds near 85-90%.
The ECB raised rates to 2.5% during the week and signalled more hikes could follow if energy prices stay elevated, a hawkish tone echoed by Bundesbank chief Nagel.
US Treasury yields climbed toward 5%, their highest since 2023, as sticky inflation data firmed up bets on further Fed tightening and rattled bond markets worldwide.

Wall Street swung sharply through the week: the Dow fell over 1,600 points across four sessions on oil and yield worries before rebounding as inflation data steadied nerves and crude eased back from its highs.

The European Commission sent the landmark EU-India free trade deal to its council for signature, while Brics nations flagged unilateral tariffs as a global risk, as India hosted the BRICS summit in New Delhi over the weekend.

standfirst: A surge in crude oil on West Asia security fears was the week's dominant story, dragging Indian equities to a fifth consecutive weekly loss, weakening the rupee and pushing India's bond yields above 7%. The RBI spent the week draining surplus banking-system liquidity and defending the rupee, even as forex reserves hit a record. Globally, hot US inflation flipped market expectations from a Fed rate cut to a near-certain hike, with the ECB striking a similarly hawkish tone.
title: Oil shock drives Sensex and Nifty to a fifth straight weekly loss as Fed turns hawkish
watch: The Fed's September 16-17 meeting, where markets now lean toward a rate hike rather than a cut.
Whether Brent crude holds below $105 or reignites the sell-off in Indian equities and the rupee.
RBI's MPC review in October, with inflation near 5% and bond yields above 7% narrowing the case for a rate cut.
The rupee's ability to hold above 95.5 to the dollar if oil and global yields stay elevated.
